title: chatglm model convert to tensorrt error
body:
## Description

<!-- A clear and concise description of the bug or issue. -->


## Environment

**TensorRT Version**:  22.12
**NVIDIA GPU**:  A30


## Relevant Files
this is my model : [https://github.com/wangzhaode/ChatGLM-MNN/releases/download/v0.4/glm_block_0.onnx](url)


## Steps To Reproduce
I use onnx-simplifier tools optimizer that glm_block_0.onnx model,  [https://github.com/daquexian/onnx-simplifier](url):
```shell
onnxsim glm_block_0.onnx glm_block_0_sim.onnx
```
we can get glm_block_0_sim.onnx model file.

then I use trtexec tool to convert model:
```shell
trtexec --onnx=glm_block_0_sim.onnx --saveEngine=glm_block_0_sim.plan 
```

but I met error:
```shell
[04/04/2023-02:33:03] [I] [TRT] ----------------------------------------------------------------
[04/04/2023-02:33:04] [W] [TRT] parsers/onnx/onnx2trt_utils.cpp:375: Your ONNX model has been generated with INT64 weights, while TensorRT does not natively support INT64. Attempting to cast down to INT32.
[04/04/2023-02:33:04] [W] [TRT] parsers/onnx/onnx2trt_utils.cpp:403: One or more weights outside the range of INT32 was clamped
[04/04/2023-02:33:04] [E] [TRT] parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:726: While parsing node number 34 [Squeeze -> "cos"]:
[04/04/2023-02:33:04] [E] [TRT] parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:727: --- Begin node ---
[04/04/2023-02:33:04] [E] [TRT] parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:728: input: "onnx::Squeeze_460"
output: "cos"
name: "Squeeze_102"
op_type: "Squeeze"
doc_string: "  File \"/home/yanxing/.cache/huggingface/modules/transformers_modules/THUDM/chatglm-6b/2449bdc9d85103734ae987bdc94eafa7fec2145d/modeling_chatglm.py\", line 196\ndef apply_rotary_pos_emb_index(q, k, cos, sin, position_id):\n    # position_id: [sq, b], q, k: [sq, b, np, hn], cos: [sq, 1, hn] -> [sq, b, 1, hn]\n    cos = torch.squeeze(cos)\n          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~ <--- HERE\n    sin = torch.squeeze(sin)\n    cos = F.embedding(position_id, cos).unsqueeze(2)\n"

[04/04/2023-02:33:04] [E] [TRT] parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:729: --- End node ---
[04/04/2023-02:33:04] [E] [TRT] parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:731: ERROR: parsers/onnx/builtin_op_importers.cpp:4793 In function importSqueeze:
[8] Assertion failed: !isDynamic(shape) && "Cannot infer squeeze dimensions from a dynamic shape! Please re-export your model with the Squeeze axes input set."
[04/04/2023-02:33:04] [E] Failed to parse onnx file
[04/04/2023-02:33:04] [I] Finish parsing network model
[04/04/2023-02:33:04] [E] Parsing model failed

&&&& FAILED TensorRT.trtexec [TensorRT v8501] # trtexec --onnx=glm_block_0_sim.onnx --saveEngine=glm_block_0_sim.plan
```

how to fix that? thank you very much.

comments.author: vanewu
comments.body: @zhaohb  chatglm should use the glm6b model. The implementation structure of this model they published cannot be directly translated to TRT. Such as 2D rotary embedding（I think your wrong counter is here） and some other  calculations implemented by himself. You need to manually modify some torch implementations of this model before converting. This may take some time on your part.

comments.author: zerollzeng
comments.body:
> ```shell
> [8] Assertion failed: !isDynamic(shape) && "Cannot infer squeeze dimensions from a dynamic shape! Please re-export your model with the Squeeze axes input set."
> ```

check the `Squeeze_102` in Netron. looks like your model is exported with dynamic shapes but it only supports fixed shape for some operator.

comments.author: zhaohb
comments.body: @vanewu @zerollzeng yes, have some op that tensorrt can not support, will tensorrt support chatglm in the future？

comments.author: vanewu
comments.body: @zhaohb Currently, the operators provided by ONNX and TensorRT are sufficient to support GLM conversion. I think a better way is to modify the source code of GLM Torch. In fact, that code also needs to be modified more, although your ONNX conversion is successful. But I guess there should be problems with numerical calculations, because many of chatglm's forward calculations pass in python built-in types, which will be converted to constants.

comments.author: zhaohb
nvpohanh
comments.body: Or try const-folding the ONNX file after you have exported it: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT/tree/main/tools/Polygraphy/examples/cli/surgeon/02_folding_constants

comments.author: vanewu
comments.body: @zhaohb It only needs to modify part of the code implementation of inference(not training) with supported operations. This does not affect the calculation results, what you probably need to modify is the position calculated by the 2D rotary embedding. If you do not modify their inference code, your ONNX calculation results should also be wrong （Even if you can convert out an onnx model). Because if you look closely at their infer code, you will find that many of the input are not tensor, and some variable values will be traced as constant values ​​for the first transmission after ONNX conversion.

comments.author: jinluyang
comments.body:
> @vanewu modify source code of GLM Torch may be not a good solution, this means we need to change the training code.
> 
> @zerollzeng
> 
> > check the Squeeze_102 in Netron. looks like your model is exported with dynamic shapes but it only supports fixed shape for some operator.
> 
> Can we also understand that tensorrt's squeeze operator does not support dynamic input, can we fix it?

I saw your message in a Wechat group that we share, let me explain to you why this isn't a Tensorrt bug. When you use cos.squeeze(1)， （that is the part of the chatglm code)， the meaning of squeeze() is it checks the 1st dimenstion, if it is 1, the dimenstion will be squeezed. otherwise it will be saved. In our case, with dynamic shape considered, the ONNX parser cannot decide if this dimension is 1 or not. So it asks you to re-export. I have also encountered this problem. You should rewrite the code as:
`cos = torch.flatten(cos,start_dim=1, end_dim=2)`
 Maybe some day I have time, I shall open a PR for those codes to the THU code..

comments.author: jinluyang
comments.body: But maybe from another perspective, there are some enhancement that can be done by TRT ONNX parser. Since the onnxruntime CPU EP does not complain about this particular issue. If TRT can deduce that this dimension is always 1 through more effective shape inferencing, it would save us a lot of time.

comments.body:
@zhaohb use python api , I use `pip install tensorrt` ，can't make trtexec.

```python
TRT_LOGGER = trt.Logger(trt.Logger.WARNING)
runtime = trt.Runtime(TRT_LOGGER)

with open(model_path, "rb") as f:
    engine = runtime.deserialize_cuda_engine(f.read())
context = engine.create_execution_context()

input_ids = np.asarray([[     5,  74874, 130001, 130004]])
position_ids = np.asarray([[[0, 1, 2, 2],
        [0, 0, 0, 1]]])
attention_mask = np.asarray([[[[False, False, False,  True],
        [False, False, False,  True],
        [False, False, False,  True],
        [False, False, False, False]]],])
context.set_binding_shape(engine.get_binding_index("input_ids"), (1, 4))
context.set_binding_shape(engine.get_binding_index("position_ids"), (1, 2, 4))
context.set_binding_shape(engine.get_binding_index("attention_mask"), (1, 1, 4, 4))

# input
bindings = []
stream = cuda.Stream()
input_ids_buffer = input_ids
input_ids_memory = cuda.mem_alloc(input_ids.nbytes)
bindings.append(int(input_ids_memory))
cuda.memcpy_htod_async(input_ids_memory, input_ids_buffer, stream)

position_ids_buffer = position_ids
position_ids_memory = cuda.mem_alloc(position_ids.nbytes)
bindings.append(int(position_ids_memory))
cuda.memcpy_htod_async(position_ids_memory, position_ids_buffer, stream)

attention_mask_buffer = attention_mask
attention_mask_memory = cuda.mem_alloc(attention_mask.nbytes)
bindings.append(int(attention_mask_memory))
cuda.memcpy_htod_async(attention_mask_memory, attention_mask_buffer, stream)

# output
output_binding = "logits"
binding_idx = engine.get_binding_index(output_binding)

size = trt.volume(context.get_binding_shape(binding_idx))
dtype = trt.nptype(engine.get_binding_dtype(output_binding))
output_buffer = cuda.pagelocked_empty(size, dtype)
output_memory = cuda.mem_alloc(output_buffer.nbytes)
bindings.append(int(output_memory))

# run
context.execute_async_v2(bindings=bindings, stream_handle=stream.handle)

cuda.memcpy_dtoh_async(output_buffer, output_memory, stream)

stream.synchronize()

output = np.reshape(output_buffer,(1,output_buffer.shape[0]//130528,130528))
print(output_buffer)
print(output_buffer.shape)
print(output_buffer.nbytes)
print(output_buffer.dtype)
print(output)
print(output.shape)
print(output.dtype)
```
